Negotiation paragraphs used by agreement announcements, DF 53.16 native PE

This is an offline reconstruction of the configured executable instructions.
It records source operands and control flow, not a game-display observation.
No game was launched, attached, or controlled; no translator was executed.

Images and function extents
  reference: data/runtime/native-pe-images.json.reference
    SHA-256 205770918fd54c96cbbcf89223ebd449e2e113c7c873ed81177c4511a3450db7
    entry RVA 0x2a71e0; executable RET RVA 0x2a8080
    PE unwind extent ends at 0x2a81ec and includes four switch tables.
  classic: data/runtime/native-pe-images.json.classic
    SHA-256 f35bbaf37aa96f93f95f8a35a9341e6649da46bc29a8650316bfdc2dfc57f3e4
    entry RVA 0x2a4da0; executable RET RVA 0x2a5c40
    PE unwind extent ends at 0x2a5dac and includes the same four tables.
  The classic constructor coordinates are reference coordinates minus 0x2440.
  Both full disassemblies are saved beside this file. Bytes after the RET are
  table data, not additional executed instruction branches.

Extraction
  PE .pdata boundaries and RIP-relative literal operands were read through the
  existing tools/extract_legends_catalog.py NativeImage implementation.
  The fixed native w64devkit-2.9.1/bin/objdump.exe produced Intel x86-64 listings.
  native-literals.tsv retains all 123 literal reference sites in each function,
  including repeated spaces, separators, and suffixes; literals are not scanned
  from nearby unrelated pools. native-switches.tsv decodes all 90 entries per
  image from four 32-bit image-relative target tables, including default aliases.

Record fields (all offsets below are from RCX, the negotiation_resultst)
  +0x00 int32 initiator historical figure; +0x04 initiator entity
  +0x08 int32 target historical figure; +0x0c target entity
  +0x10 int32 target position ID; +0x14 target position entity
  +0x18 int16 meeting topic; +0x1c int32 result
  +0x20 int32 result site ID; +0x24 int32 result magnitude
  +0x28 int32 initiator negotiation roll; +0x2c initiator persuasion roll
  +0x30 int32 initiator extra skill; +0x34 initiator extra-skill roll
  +0x38 int32 target negotiation roll; +0x3c target JUDGMENT roll
  +0x40 int32 target extra skill; +0x44 int32 target extra-skill roll
  +0x48 vector<int32> difficulty modifier kinds
  +0x60 vector<int32> difficulty modifier values, indexed with the kinds
  The structural names also appear in data/upstream/df-structures/df.history.xml.
  +0x3c is judgment, not a second persuasion roll. The two sides are asymmetric.

Identity and affiliation (0x2a7231..0x2a73ff)
  The initiator and target are formatted by historical figure helper 0xb92f10.
  The initiator is capitalized by 0x52d650; the initial target is not capitalized.
  The strategy sentences format both figures again, capitalizing each.
  These are complete generated historical-figure identities, not arbitrary
  single-name tokens. No current-save names are enumerated in the catalogue.
  Entity names are produced by 0xb92900; site by 0xb93930.

  initiator_entity == -1: FIGURE
  otherwise: FIGURE + " of " + ENTITY

  target_entity == -1: FIGURE
  target position ID == -1, or position entity/vector/position lookup missing:
    FIGURE + " of " + TARGET_ENTITY
  successful position lookup (entity positions +0x10c0, ID +0x20):
    FIGURE + ", " + neutral singular POSITION_TITLE(+0x98)
      + " of " + POSITION_ENTITY
    if position_entity != target_entity:
      append ", representing " + TARGET_ENTITY
    append ","
  A found position with an empty neutral title stays on this branch. It must
  not be inferred to be a missing position from title.empty().

Meeting purpose (0x2a73ff..0x2a747e)
  Always: INITIATOR + " met with " + TARGET
  Topic 1: append " to make peace"
  Topic 10: append " to demand unconditional surrender"
  Topic 14: append " to seek an alliance"
  Topic 15: append " to make contact and open trade"
  Topic 16: append " to improve trade relations"
  Every other topic: append no purpose
  Always append "."

Firm siege morale (0x2a7483..0x2a74ba)
  result == 2:
    append "  The negotiation was doomed to failure while the morale of the invaders sieging "
      + SITE(+0x20) + " held firm."
    jump to the common append at 0x2a8048, then return.
  This branch does not reach difficulty, strategy, response, or proposal text.

Difficulty sequence (0x2a74bf..0x2a7679), for every kind/value pair in order
  kind 0 and value < 0:
    append "  The "
    value <= -150: "sheer number of lost invaders"
    value <= -75: "great number of lost invaders"
    value <= -25: "high number of lost invaders"
    otherwise: "enemy losses during invasions"
    append " made the task seem more possible."
  kind 1 and value > 0:
    append "  The task was made "
    value >= 75: "much more difficult"
    value >= 50: "more difficult"
    otherwise: "somewhat more difficult"
    append " by the relative populations of the civilizations."
  kind 2 and value < 0:
    append "  The task was made "
    value <= -100: "much easier"
    value <= -80: "easier"
    otherwise: "somewhat easier"
    append " by the relative populations of the civilizations."
  All other kind/sign combinations append no text.

Opening strategy (0x2a768c..0x2a799e)
  Append "  " + capitalized INITIATOR + " ".
  result == 1: "attempted to"; all other results: "began to".
  Append " ". Set remembered opening style to signed int16 as noted below.
  N=+0x28, P=+0x2c, S=+0x30, R=+0x34.
  Comparisons are signed int32; 2*P and 2*R use native wrapping int32 arithmetic.

  N >= P and N >= R:
    remembered style=71; auxiliary=-1
    if 2*P >= N: auxiliary=70
    if 2*R >= N and R > P: auxiliary=signed int16(S)
    auxiliary switch at table 0x2a8084, range 70..92:
      70 "negotiate persuasively"
      72 "negotiate with discernment"
      76 "negotiate deceptively"
      77 "negotiate forcefully"
      78 "negotiate amidst light conversation"
      79 "negotiate, keeping a sense of humor"
      80 "negotiate, mixing in a dose of flattery"
      81 "negotiate with empathy for their counterpart"
      82 "negotiate calmly"
      92 "negotiate eloquently"
      all others "negotiate"
  Otherwise if P >= R:
    remembered style=70; append "argue persuasively"
  Otherwise:
    remembered style=signed int16(S); full int32 S controls table 0x2a80e0:
      72 "feel out intentions and argue" +
           (result==0 ? " with subtlety" : " carefully")
      76 "brazenly lie"
      77 "intimidate their adversary"
      78 "make conversation to set a mood"
      79 "use humor to disarm their opponent"
      80 "flatter their counterpart"
      81 "appeal to shared history and show empathy"
      82 "calm any misgivings about the proposal"
      92 "make a rousing speech"
      all others append no strategy (the sentence retains "began to ." or
        "attempted to ."). S=70/71 are also on this default branch.
  Append ".  ".

Response strategy (0x2a79a3..0x2a7f76)
  Append capitalized TARGET + " ".
  N=+0x38, J=+0x3c, S=+0x40, R=+0x44; success=(result==0).
  N >= J and N >= R:
    auxiliary=-1
    if 2*J >= N: auxiliary=72 (judgment, not initiator's 70)
    if 2*R >= N and R > J: auxiliary=signed int16(S)
    switch table 0x2a8134, range 70..92:
      70 "negotiated persuasively"
      72 "negotiated with discernment"
      76 "negotiated deceptively"
      77 "negotiated forcefully"
      78 "negotiated lightly"
      79 "negotiated with humor"
      80 "negotiated with flattery"
      81 "negotiated with empathy"
      82 "negotiated calmly"
      92 "negotiated eloquently"
      all others "negotiated"
    if remembered opening style==71: append " in turn"
    success: " but was outmaneuvered"; otherwise: " and had the mastery"
  Otherwise if J >= R:
    success: "attempted to read"; otherwise: "read"
    append " their opposite's underlying motivations"
    if remembered opening style==72: append " as well"
    if success: append " but was swept along"
  Otherwise, full int32 S controls table 0x2a8190, range 70..92:
    matched=(remembered opening style==signed int16(S))
    70 "made a persuasive argument"
       if matched: " of their own"
       if success: " but was ultimately swayed"
    76 "spun a web of deceit"
       if matched: " of their own"
       if success: " but became tied in their own knots"
    77 "intimidated their opposite"
       if matched: " with matching fury"
       if success: " but grew meeker throughout the proceedings"
    78 matched ? "joined the conversation" : "made light conversation"
       success ? " and over time came around on the matter"
               : " and skillfully shut down the proceedings"
    79 "made several jokes"
       if matched: " of their own"
       success ? " but came to see the seriousness of the issue at hand"
               : " and dismissed the matter"
    80 matched ? "flattered their opposite in turn" : "made a great show of flattery"
       success ? " and ultimately agreed" : " but left the matter unaddressed"
    81 matched ? "joined in the discussion of history and past griefs"
               : "showed empathy with their opposite"
       success ? " and agreed on the issue" : " but did not agree"
    82 "attempted to put their opposite at ease"
       if matched: " as well"
       success ? " and ultimately agreed" : " but did not ultimately agree"
    92 matched ? "replied with a grand oration of their own" : "replied with a fiery speech"
       if success: " but ultimately the matter was agreed"
    all others append no response; specifically S=72 also takes this default.
  The common continuation appends ".  The proposal ".

Proposal result (0x2a7c4a..0x2a804b)
  result==1, magnitude +0x24:
    -5 "was a spectacular failure"
    -4 "was a resounding failure"
    -3 "was an embarrassing failure"
    -2 "was a failure"
    all other magnitudes "was not successful"
  result==0, magnitude +0x24:
     5 "was wildly successful beyond any expectations"
     4 "was a truly grand success"
     3 "was a great success"
     2 "was highly successful"
     all other magnitudes "succeeded"
  Other results (2 already returned before this block): append no predicate.
    The native default is exactly "The proposal .".
  Append ".", destroy temporary strings, and return.

Translation consumers
  data/runtime/announcement-negotiation-grammar.tsv holds complete Chinese
  templates for every finite wording, optional echo, success/failure combination,
  and empty-predicate default. Historical figure captures use $historical-actor;
  entities/sites reuse generated name semantics; position titles use $office.
  src/native_history_diplomacy.inc captures typed fields and true position presence.
  src/history_semantics_diplomacy.inc selects the same branches from typed fields,
  including the asymmetric target judgment, siege early return, 32-bit skill
  dispatch vs 16-bit style memory, and all native empty predicates.
